newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporations sell over $1 bln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporations sell over $1 bln in bonds.

text.p: Lured by recent interest rate declines, U.S. corporations sold over $1 billion in investment grade bonds on Wednesday as of midday with more issuance seen on the way, according to syndicate officials.

"This rally is quite incredible and the street will be very fast to respond. Many issuers which have shelves in place are likely to quickly tap the market to gain access to favorable rates," a syndicate source said.
And the fast pace is expected to continue through the week.

Banque Nationale de Paris plans to sell $350 million in A1/A-rated 12-year subordinated notes through Salomon Brothers either today or tomorrow, sources said. Price talk was 80-82 basis points over the 10-year Treasury, they added.
Levi Strauss & Co is also rumored to be readying a private placement 144a offering through Goldman Sachs & Co.
Earlier Wednesday, Ford Motor Co sold $500 million in debentures and Praxair Inc sold $250 million in notes.
This morning, May Department stores sold $125 million of debt and Heller Financial sold $200 million in notes.
With investors focused on new issues, traders say secondary market trading among invesment grade bonds was particularly light.
In the high-yield sector, secondary market activity was more lively, with bonds trading 1/4 point higher across many sectors.
Ralphs Grocery Co bonds weakened one to two points on news released on Wednesday that Safeway Inc has offered to purchase The Vons Companies Inc, a large food retailer in Southen California.
"This is going to create an even tougher competitor for Ralphs," a trader said

Nextel Communications Inc bonds tightened by 15 to 25 basis points on Wednesday, following a conference for analysts and investors on Tuesday in which the company unveiled its new communiations technology, traders say
